newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Jan 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Jan 21.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Fidel Ramos drops broad hints that he is disappointed with the failure of police to capture congressman Romeo Jalosjos for 23 days, saying he is evaluating the performance of all govenment officials, including that of police chief Recaredo Sarmiento. (ALL PAPERS)
- Senate president Ernesto Maceda says a minority bloc in the Senate is plotting a coup to oust him from his post (MANILA STANDARD)
- House leaders say they will not accept the 9.0 billion peso insertion made by the senators in the proposed 1997 budget bill. (PHILIPPINE JOURNAL)
- Families in southern Davao del Norte and Agusan del Sur provinces have been evacuated to higher ground because of rising floodwaters in the two provinces. (MANILA BULLETIN)
- The National Capital Region's tripartite wage and productivity board is set to approve a 20 peso increase in the present minimum wage of 165 pesos a day. (BUSINESSWORLD)

- The multi-sectoral tax council intends to propose to Congress the imposition of a 10 percent creditable witholding tax in lieu of the current 20 percent final tax on financial instruments. (BUSINESS DAILY)

- The country posted a balance of payment surplus of $3.7 billion in the first three quarters of last year, or about five times the $783 million surplus in the same period in 1995. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)
